name: Outlook hash leak
tile_line: Exploited via crafted files. On CISA's exploited list.
tldr: Opening a crafted Office file in classic Outlook hands the user's NTLMv2 hash to an attacker, who can sign in as them. Exploited, on CISA's exploited list. Install the 10 Nov 2026 Office update: Windows updates alone don't fix it.
summary: The crafted file makes Outlook connect to the attacker's server without its usual warning, and that connection carries the user's NTLMv2 hash.

affected.label: Classic Outlook from a listed Office
affected.text: Microsoft lists Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Office LTSC 2024 and Office LTSC 2021, 32- and 64-bit; retail Office 2021 and 2024 get the same Current Channel fix. Office Watch says new Outlook for Windows isn't affected and Outlook for Mac isn't on Microsoft's list.

affected.label: Build older than the 10 Nov 2026 fix
A user opens the malicious file
affected.text: The attacker has to get the user to open a crafted message or Office file. Microsoft says the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

do.label: Update Office, not just Windows
do.text: The fix comes through Office's own updater, not a Windows cumulative update. In any Office app: File > Office Account > Update Options > Update Now, then restart Outlook. Admins: make sure your channel has reached the builds above (Intune, Configuration Manager or your Office update source).

do.label: Retire Office 2016 and 2019
do.text: Microsoft doesn't list Office 2016 or 2019 for this CVE, though Office 2019 volume-licensed builds did get a 10 Nov update (1808, build 10417.20236). Office Watch assumes they're affected. Both are out of support: move those users to a supported Office.

do.label: Until patched: warn users
do.text: Microsoft lists no workaround. Tell users not to open unexpected message or Office attachments, and lean on your email gateway. Microsoft hasn't published indicators of compromise.
